notes.decision: Translated as 'taming.' Recurs at lines 5 and 13 as the structurally pivotal phrase ⲧⲇⲁⲙ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the taming of the Mind of Light' marking the turn from BEFORE to NOW. Likely from Greek δάμασις/δαμάζω 'tame, subdue,' fitting the Manichaean doctrine of the Light-Mind subduing the body's passions. Alternative: Coptic ⲧⲱⲙ 'shut, bind' (cf. line 26 'bound them in a bond of peace'). 'Taming' preserves the active subjugation semantics.

Parsed as ⲡⲉⲧⲁϩ- (perfect relative 'who has') + reduplicated verb (ϩ)ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲗⲱⲙ̄/ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ 'trample, defile' (in glossary as ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ/ϩⲟⲗⲙⲗⲱⲙⲥ̄) + 3pl object suffix -ⲩ. Translation 'who has trampled them down' fits the soteriological subjugation of the body's desires.

Translated 'the tyrant of the body.' Likely Lyc. nativized form of Greek τύραννος, with vowel-shift τυραν > ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲣⲉ. Apposition with ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ 'desire' identifies desire as the tyrant whom the Mind of Light has now humbled.

Translated 'have fled.' Recurs at line 15 (ⲁⲩⲣⲃⲁⲧⲉ 'they fled'). Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱⲧ 'do running, flee' or related to ⲡⲱⲱⲧⲉ 'leap.' Soteriological-cosmological motif: phantasies of desire and evil mysteries flee at the coming of the Mind of Light.

Translated 'persuasions.' Etymology uncertain — possibly Greek πειθώ 'persuasion' or πάθος 'passion' with Lyc. orthographic adaptation. Parallel with preceding ⲟⲩⲭⲗⲉ (= ὄχλος 'noise/crowd') of desire suggests an auditory-affective register. 'Persuasions' captures the seductive-rhetorical force fitting the ear-faculty context.

Translated 'it pleases (him) not at all ... it pleases (him).' The form ⲉⲍⲛⲉϩ likely from ϩⲛⲁ⸗ 'be pleased, wish' as impersonal predicate with ⲉⲛ negation. Antithetical pair structuring the contrast: hearings of desire are no longer welcome, voices of psalms are now welcome at every hour.

Translated 'songs.' Position between ⲡⲥⲁⲗⲙⲟⲥ 'psalms' and ⲍⲩⲙⲛⲟⲥ 'hymns' parallels the canonical NT triad ψαλμοί / ὕμνοι / ᾠδαί (Eph 5:19, Col 3:16). Possible Greek source: ᾠδαί 'songs/odes,' though phonological mapping is irregular. Could alternatively be a Coptic-specific liturgical term for antiphons/responses.

Translated 'one set above it.' Probable parsing ⲡⲉⲧ-ϩⲓ-ϫⲱ-ϥ̄ 'the one upon him,' i.e. 'overseer, restrainer.' The Manichaean theme: under the body's pre-conversion regime, Sin reigned with no one to restrain it; now the Living Spirit has become its lord (line 25).

Translated 'the first and the last.' Refers to Sin's former dominion as totality 'from beginning to end,' setting up the antithesis with the Holy Spirit's purpose-of-heart in line 32. Could alternatively be construed as a temporal partition: 'Sin's purpose was the first (former state); and (now) the purpose of the Holy Spirit (is) the last (final state) joined to the gnōmē of the Mind of Light.'

Retained as 'gnōmē' (Greek γνώμη 'judgment, mind, will'). Manichaean technical sense: the rational-judging will of the Mind of Light, which now governs in place of Sin's purpose-of-heart. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ (purpose) and ⲙⲉⲩⲉ (thought).
